summary: High sustained p95/p99 latency in dedicated pool during customer's nightly small-stream embedding sweep; connection leak suspected
description: Issue summary: Customer LensAI reports a progressive degradation in tail latency (p95/p99) and throughput in their dedicated GPU pool during a nightly embedding sweep that issues many short-lived embedding requests. Impact: Customer's batch job (embedding sweep for 6M items) now runs 3x longer and stalls downstream pipelines. Environment: Dedicated pool (LensAI-reserved-3) in prod-us-west-2, routing to embedding-small-v2; issue first observed on 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run ~2000 concurrent short embedding requests (payloads ~512 bytes) with keep-alive disabled/closed quickly; 2) Observe allocator slot counts, connection table, and short-stream fanout; 3) Notice increasing queue depth and autoscaler failing to attach additional GPUs. Observed behavior: - p50 stable, p95/p99 and tail CPU/GPU attach times increase gradually over 1–2 hours. - Node/socket table shows many TIME_WAIT/FIN_WAIT entries. - Autoscaler metrics show attach attempts succeeding but effective usable slots falling due to connections occupying scheduler slots. Initial hypothesis: Customer client opens very high concurrency of short-lived connections without proper connection pooling/keep-alive, leading to ephemeral socket churn that ties up scheduler/sidecar resources (prefetch and per-connection state), causing allocator fragmentation and autoscaler misinterpretation (appears as slot capacity but unavailable). Attachments/Logs: - Support logs: /var/log/support/SUP-246801/support_debug_2026-03-10.tar.gz - Grafana dashboard snapshots: tail_latency_spike_2026-03-10.png - Packet capture excerpt available on request. Requested customer action: Provide client HTTP connection settings and a short reproducible script.

Reproduced locally with a synthetic short-stream script. Opening 2K concurrent short connections produces similar TIME_WAIT accumulation and p99 drift.

2026-03-10 14:21 - LensAI engineer (customer): Confirmed client used no connection pooling; their current SDK creates a new TCP connection per request. They attached a representative load generator (script). Asked whether Redwood can throttle per-tenant connection creation.

Plan: schedule patch to sidecar to aggressively recycle per-connection state and add heuristics for short-lived-connection flood detection. Linked PR and runbook added.
investigation_notes: Sidecar analysis: sidecar process holds per-connection prefetch metadata in memory for up to 30s after close; with high churn this accumulates and blocks slot reclamation.
Kernel socket state: large number of sockets in TIME_WAIT and FIN_WAIT2 observed on nodes; OS tcp_tw_reuse and ephemeral port exhaustion risk considered but not reached.
Autoscaler behavior: attach attempt rate healthy, but scheduler marks slots as in-use because per-connection prefetch leases exist; this prevents immediate reuse leading to effective capacity drop.
Customer pattern: high qps of very short requests (~10–50ms server time) with no pooling; SDK defaults identified as root trigger.
Load reproduction: synthetic generator reproduced p99 drift in lab at ~1800 concurrent short streams. Enabling HTTP/2 multiplexing eliminated drift in test.
Risk assessment: If left unmitigated, can cause other tenants in same reserved pool to observe intermittent p99 regressions during large short-stream campaigns.
Workarounds tried: per-pool soft-rate-limiter (reduced immediate impact), temporary increase of prefetch reclamation aggressiveness (reclaimed slots but raised minor p50 jitter).
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigations applied 2026-03-11: per-pool connection soft cap and autoscaler sensitivity window increased. Customer validated ~45% job time improvement.

Planned actions: 1) Sidecar patch to aggressively free per-connection prefetch state and detect short-connection floods (PR linked). 2) Scheduler tweak to treat recently-closed prefetch leases as reclaimable under short-stream flood condition. 3) Add tenant-level guidance in docs and provide SDK patch sample to LensAI to enable persistent connections/HTTP/2.
Customer communication: Provided concrete SDK config recommendations and sample patch to switch to HTTP/2 multiplexing. Follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-13 to validate final throughput.
Owner: Miguel Santos (SRE) to own sidecar/scheduler changes; ETA for durable patch: 2026-03-19 (pending review).
outcome: Mitigated with soft-rate-limiter and guidance; durable sidecar/scheduler patches in progress. Customer to validate nightly run; postmortem and KB to follow once patch is deployed.
